resources.string: On-device capabilities the agent may use

Each toggle is standing consent: the agent can only invoke a tool that is switched on here. Tools that need an Android permission still fail closed until the permission is granted — a toggle on its own is never enough.

Invocations are explicit. LEVI never reads location, opens apps, or fetches URLs silently in the background — each of these runs only when the agent calls the tool, and every result reports honestly whether the action happened.
Notifications posted by LEVI\'s on-device tools when the agent asks it to notify you.
Posts a notification on this device with a title and body.
Opens the system calendar editor pre-filled with the event.
No calendar permission needed: the system editor opens and you confirm the event on screen.
Hands an alarm or countdown timer to the system clock app.
Returns a coarse network/IP-based position estimate.
City-block level at best. Read only at the moment of invocation — never tracked in the background.
Opens an http(s) link in the default browser.
Opens a file from the app\'s own storage in its default app.
Scoped to LEVI\'s own storage; paths outside it are refused.
Returns the device\'s current time, timezone and UTC offset.
Hands a query to the device\'s default search handler.
Fetches an HTTPS URL and returns the body text to the agent.
HTTPS only — plain HTTP is refused. Responses are capped in size and time.
